SUBJECT: 2025 YEAR IN REVIEW AND UPDATE ON PLANNING DIVISION
RESPONSIBILITIES AND PROCEDURES

PURPOSE: To provide the Planning Commission with a recap of projects reviewed in 2025, and
provide an update on division responsibilities and procedures.

BACKGROUND:
The Planning Division is responsible for processing development applications in the City based
on the zoning regulations found in Title 11 of the South Gate Municipal Code. The City has
established several zones, each with its own development standards. These zones are grouped into
three broad categories: urban mixed-use zones, commercial industrial zones, and residential
neighborhood zones. Many types of projects can be approved by staff at the administrative level.
However, certain projects and land uses require discretionary review by the Planning Commission.
These include conditional use permits, variances, and site plan reviews. Actions by staff
(Community Development Director) are appealable to the Planning Commission, and actions by
the Planning Commission are appealable to the City Council.

ANALYSIS:

Planning Counter
The Community Development Department uses QLess as an electronic sign-in for customers at
the front counter. The system was implemented after the start of the pandemic to limit contact
between customers and staff. Customers are able to sign in electronically, wait in their cars or in
the lobby, and be summoned to the counter when they are next in line. The Community
Development Department provides services at the front counter for Planning, Building and Safety,
Code Enforcement, and Housing. QLess makes it easy to track the number of customers coming
to the front counter and to transfer or refer customers to another division.

In 2025, there were a total of 9,003 customers who came to the Community Development
Department counter. This averages about 750 customers per month. Roughly 93.9% of customers
proceed with their appointments; the others are removed (either on their own or by another
division), leave, or do not show up. Figure 1 summarizes the number of customers served by the
Community Development Department in 2025.

Planning Projects
Planning applications are submitted electronically when applicants email completed applications
and plans to the Planning Division’s email account. The Planning Division tracks all development
projects using an online software system, EdgeSoft. Upon receipt, staff assigns a PL (Planning)
case number to each development application.

In 2025, staff recorded 489 cases, including 213 accessory dwelling units (ADUs), 16 junior
ADUs, 28 accessory structure permits, 34 design reviews, and seven conditional use permits
(CUPs), among others. Simple applications, such as roof repairs, roof-mounted solar panels, and
interior remodels, are typically processed quickly. More complex or questionable applications may
require several weeks for review.

For projects requiring administrative review, applications are received electronically, and the
assigned planner has 30 days under the Permit Streamlining Act to notify the applicant whether
the application is complete. Plans are also routed to other departments—including Building, Public
Works, Police, and Fire—for review and comment. If an application is deemed incomplete, the
planner provides written notification to the applicant identifying missing items and noting any
discrepancies with applicable development standards.

For discretionary projects, such as CUPs and variances that require Planning Commission
approval, the planner similarly reviews the application for completeness and compliance within
the initial 30-day period. Once the application is complete, the planner prepares the project for a
public hearing before the Planning Commission. Public notices are published in the newspaper
and mailed to property owners and residents within 1,000 feet of the project site.

The typical timeframe to schedule a Planning Commission hearing is approximately four to six
months, provided the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
If the project is not exempt and requires preparation of a Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND)

(LLA), and three appeals. Most of these applications were reviewed by the Planning Commission

Throughout the year, workshops were presented to the Planning Commission, which included
presentations on the Brown Act, permit types and responsibilities, signage, a brownfield grant,
CEQA, and the City’s budget. These were informational items that the Planning Commission
received and filed.

In June 2025, the Planning Commission conducted a reorganization to select a new chairperson
and vice chairperson. This is typically done each year at the end of the fiscal year.

CONCLUSION:
Staff continues to make improvements to better serve residents and the development community.
Despite a high volume of projects in 2025, staff managed workloads while dealing with vacancies.
As the City moves into 2026, staff remains committed to addressing challenges, enhancing
operational efficiency, and providing customer-friendly service to the community.

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Planning Commission receive the presentation, ask questions of staff,
open the item for public comment, and RECEIVE and FILE the item.

SUBJECT: WORKSHOP ON CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS FOR ALCOHOL SALES
FROM 2023-2025

PURPOSE: To provide the Planning Commission with an update on conditional use permits
(CUPs) issued for alcohol sales over the past three years.

BACKGROUND: Since 2023, the Planning Commission has issued 9 CUPs for alcohol sales as
shown in Table 1 (Attachment A). Six of those CUPs deal with Type 41 licenses for on-sale beer
and wine, two deal with a Type 47 for on-sale general eating place, one deals with a Type 20 for
off-sale beer and wine, and one business (Target retail store) was issued a license for a Type 21
(Off-sale Beer, Wine, & Distilled Spirits) and a Type 86 (instructional Tasting License) license.

Two businesses recently received approval of their CUPs and are pending licensing from the
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC). One restaurant is no longer in business and the
ABC license has been canceled.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: It is recommended that the Planning Commission receive the
presentation, ask questions of staff, open the item for public comment, and RECEIVE and FILE
the item.

SUBJECT: WORKSHOP ON UPCOMING PROJECTS

PURPOSE: To provide the Planning Commission with an overview of expected projects in 2026.

BACKGROUND: Planning staff is currently working on a number of projects. Many are
administrative and do not require a public hearing. Projects that require a conditional use permit
(CUP), variance, tentative tract map (TTM), or other discretionary approval will be brought to the
Planning Commission for consideration.

Attachment A shows projects currently under review that may be scheduled for a Planning
Commission meeting in the coming months.

Attachment B is a flyer advertising an open house for the Gateway District on Wednesday,
February 18, 2026, from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m. Commissioners and the public are encouraged to attend.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: It is recommended that the Planning Commission receive the
presentation, ask questions of staff, open the item for public comment, and RECEIVE and FILE
the item.
